item.title: Ariana Grande Sues Hackers Over Leaks of Unreleased Music: ‘Unlawful and Egregious’
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest news and trends in the music industry. Today, we're talking about Ariana Grande and her battle against hackers. Let's get into it.
[Soft music transitions in]
Host: Ariana Grande has filed a lawsuit against unnamed hackers who have been stealing and leaking her unreleased music, photos, and videos. According to her lawyers, these hackers have been targeting her team, including photographers and producers, to get their hands on her private content. In 2023 alone, 45 of her songs were stolen and leaked.
[Short pause for emphasis]
Host: Grande's lawyers argue that these hackers have been causing her significant harm, violating her privacy and disrupting her career. They've been selling her stolen content on the dark web for big bucks, and Grande is determined to unmask them. The lawsuit names "John Doe" hackers, but Grande is hoping to use the lawsuit to identify them through court-ordered subpoenas to internet service providers.
[Music transitions to a slightly more serious tone]
Host: This isn't a new problem for Grande. Her lawyers say she's faced hundreds of leaks since 2011, including a 2019 theft of unreleased music and footage, and two phishing scams in 2024 that stole her photos. Grande is suing for invasion of privacy, violation of California computer hacking laws, and conversion – the civil equivalent of theft.
[Short pause for reflection]
Host: As her lawyers put it, "The unauthorized misappropriation and disclosure of these materials is a violation of Ms. Grande's identity and artistry, and the direct and sacred relationship that exists between her and her fans." Grande is taking a stand against these hackers, and we'll be keeping an eye on this story as it develops.
[Outro music plays]
Host: Thanks for tuning in to our podcast. Join us next time for more updates on the music industry. [Outro music continues to play until the end]
